questions.question: In the 56th meeting of Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) held from 4 to 6 August 2025, real GDP growth for Q1 2026-27 was projected at:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**0.066**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **56th meeting of the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC)** was held from **4 to 6 August 2025**.
 
• During this meeting, the **real GDP growth** projection for **Q1 2026-27** was discussed.
 
• The projected **real GDP growth rate** for Q1 2026-27 was announced as **0.066 (6.6%)**.
 
• This projection reflects the **expected economic performance** in the first quarter of the fiscal year 2026-27, considering current economic trends and policy measures.
 
• The MPC's primary mandate is to ensure **price stability** while supporting growth, and such GDP projections are integral to policy decisions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Monetary Policy Committee (MPC):**

 
 
• The **MPC** was formed under the **Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934** and is responsible for fixing the benchmark interest rate in India.
 
• It consists of **6 members**, including 3 RBI officials and 3 external members appointed by the government.
 
• The MPC aims to maintain **inflation within the target range** while fostering economic growth.
 
 
 
• **Real GDP Growth:**
 
 
• **Real GDP growth** measures the economic growth rate adjusted for inflation, providing a clearer picture of the economy's performance.
 
• It is a critical indicator used by policymakers, analysts, and investors to assess economic health.
 
 
 
• **Economic Projections:**
 
 
• The RBI and MPC often release **growth projections** to inform stakeholders and adjust monetary policy accordingly.
 
• Projections are based on factors like **global economic trends, domestic inflation, fiscal policies, and geopolitical events.**
 
 
 
• **Inflation Targeting:**
 
 
• India adopted **inflation targeting** as a monetary policy framework in 2016, with the MPC tasked with maintaining inflation within a specified range.
 
• The target is **4% (+/- 2%)**, ensuring price stability while supporting growth.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **GDP Measurement:**

 
 
• **Gross Domestic Product (GDP)** is the total value of goods and services produced in a country over a specific period.
 
• It is measured in **real terms** (adjusted for inflation) and nominal terms (current prices).
 
 
 
• **Factors Influencing GDP Growth:**
 
 
• Several factors impact GDP growth, including **investment rates, consumer spending, fiscal policies, and global trade dynamics.**
 
• Unexpected events like **natural disasters, pandemics, or geopolitical tensions** can also affect growth rates.
 
 
 
• **RBI's Role:**
 
 
• The **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** plays a pivotal role in managing monetary policy to influence GDP growth and inflation.
 
• Tools like **repo rate, reverse repo rate, and cash reserve ratio** are used to regulate liquidity and credit availability in the economy.

• In 2025, she led a significant **youth movement** advocating for stronger climate actions and the implementation of policies to safeguard the environment for future generations.

• Licypriya is widely recognized for her campaign to make environmental education a mandatory subject in schools in India.
 
• At the age of 9, she was awarded the prestigious **Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam Children Award** for her remarkable contributions to environmental advocacy.

• **Global Youth Movements:**

questions.question: Which edition of International Conference on 'Arbitrating Indo-UK Commercial Disputes' was organised by the Indian Council of Arbitration (ICA)during the London International Disputes Week (LIDW) in June 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**3rd Edition**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **3rd edition** of the International Conference on 'Arbitrating Indo-UK Commercial Disputes' was organized by the **Indian Council of Arbitration (ICA)** during the **London International Disputes Week (LIDW)** in **June 2025**.
 
• The conference aimed to strengthen **India-UK arbitration relations**, focusing on resolving commercial disputes involving businesses from both nations.
 
• The event provided a platform for legal professionals, arbitrators, and business leaders to discuss the **challenges and developments** in arbitration practices between the two countries.
 
• The Indian Council of Arbitration (ICA) is a premier arbitration body in India, established to promote **alternative dispute resolution mechanisms** and ensure efficient resolution of disputes.
 
• London International Disputes Week (LIDW) is an annual event that gathers professionals from across the globe to focus on **dispute resolution developments**, including arbitration and mediation practices.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Indian Council of Arbitration (ICA):**

 
 
• Established in **1965**, ICA operates under the aegis of the Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (**FICCI**).
 
• It is responsible for promoting **arbitration** as a means of alternative dispute resolution (ADR) in India.
 
• ICA organizes **conferences, training programs, and seminars** to educate professionals about arbitration and ADR mechanisms.
 
 
 
• **London International Disputes Week (LIDW):**
 
 
• LIDW is held annually in London, UK, with participation from global legal and arbitration professionals.
 
• The event focuses on **cross-border disputes**, arbitration practices, and innovations in dispute resolution.
 
• It encourages collaboration between nations to improve arbitration frameworks and practices.
 
 
 
• **India-UK Commercial Relations:**
 
 
• The UK is one of India's **leading trade partners**, with bilateral trade valued at billions of dollars annually.
 
• Arbitration plays a critical role in resolving disputes arising from business transactions and contractual disagreements between entities in both countries.
 
• Strengthening arbitration mechanisms can improve **business confidence** and promote smoother trade relations.
 
 
 
• **Arbitration Practices:**
 
 
• Arbitration is a widely recognized and utilized method for resolving disputes outside of traditional court systems.
 
• It involves appointing neutral arbitrators who deliver legally binding decisions based on evidence and arguments presented by parties.
 
• India has adopted the **Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996**, which aligns with international standards like the **UNCITRAL Model Law**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996:**

 
 
• This Act governs arbitration proceedings in India and incorporates provisions for **domestic and international arbitration**.
 
• It aims to reduce the burden on Indian courts by encouraging **alternative dispute resolution mechanisms**.
 
 
 
• **UNCITRAL Model Law:**
 
 
• The **United Nations Commission on International Trade Law (UNCITRAL) Model Law** serves as a framework for countries to establish or reform their arbitration laws.
 
• India's Arbitration Act aligns with the **UNCITRAL standards**, ensuring international acceptance of Indian arbitration practices.
 
 
 
• **Cross-Border Arbitration:**
 
 
• Cross-border arbitration resolves disputes involving parties from different nations.
 
• It emphasizes neutrality, efficiency, and enforceability of awards under treaties like the **New York Convention**.

• A **market repo** is a short-term borrowing tool where one party sells securities to another with an agreement to repurchase them at a predetermined price and date.
 
• **Tri-Party Repo (TREP)** is a similar mechanism involving a third-party agent for collateral management, which ensures reduced settlement risks.
 
• The extension aligns with RBI's broader objective of **deepening financial markets** and encouraging more participation from stakeholders.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Market Repo:**

 
 
• This is a tool for **short-term borrowing and lending** in the money market.
 
• It involves selling securities with an agreement to repurchase them at a later date.
 
• It is used by **banks, financial institutions**, and other participants to manage liquidity needs.
 
 
 
• **Tri-Party Repo (TREP):**
 
 
• Involves a **third-party agent** (usually a clearing corporation) to manage collateral.
 
• It reduces **settlement and counterparty risks**.
 
• TREP is widely used in India for short-term borrowing and lending in the money market.
 
 
 
• **Reserve Bank of India (RBI):**
 
 
• The central bank of India, established on **1 April 1935**, headquartered in Mumbai.
 
• RBI regulates the monetary policy and ensures the **stability of the financial system**.
 
• It also oversees the functioning of payment systems and manages India's foreign exchange.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Extended Trading Hours:**
 
 
• Provides market participants with additional time to **complete transactions**.
 
• Enhances **liquidity** and allows better price discovery in the financial markets.
 
• Encourages more participation from investors, traders, and other stakeholders.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

questions.question: Which of the following institutes was chosen by the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) in January 2025 to establish South India’s first Infectious Disease Research and Diagnostic Laboratory (IRDL)?

options.text: Bangalore Medical College and Research Institute (BMCRI)
Sri Ramachandra Medical College and Research Institute, Chennai
Kamineni Academy of Medical Sciences And Research Centre, Hyderabad

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bangalore Medical College and Research Institute (BMCRI)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR)** selected the **Bangalore Medical College and Research Institute (BMCRI)** in **January 2025** to establish **South India’s first Infectious Disease Research and Diagnostic Laboratory (IRDL)**.
 
• The **IRDL** aims to enhance the capability of diagnosing and conducting advanced research on **infectious diseases**, which are a major public health concern in India.
 
• **Bangalore Medical College and Research Institute (BMCRI)**, located in **Bangalore, Karnataka**, is known for its excellence in medical education and healthcare services, making it an ideal choice for hosting this advanced facility.
 
• The laboratory will focus on addressing the challenges posed by **emerging infectious diseases** and will help in **strengthening the public health infrastructure** in the region.
 
• This initiative aligns with the **ICMR’s mission** to improve public health research and preparedness for tackling outbreaks and pandemics effectively in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **About Bangalore Medical College and Research Institute (BMCRI):**

 
 
• Founded in **1955**, BMCRI is one of the oldest and most reputed medical institutions in **Karnataka**.
 
• It is affiliated with the **Rajiv Gandhi University of Health Sciences (RGUHS)**, Karnataka.
 
• BMCRI operates several associated hospitals, including **Victoria Hospital, Bowring and Lady Curzon Hospital**, and **Vanivilas Women and Children’s Hospital**.
 
• The institute is a hub for **medical research** and training, contributing significantly to healthcare advancements in the region.
 
 
 
• **Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR):**
 
 
• Established in **1911**, ICMR is the apex body in India for the formulation, coordination, and promotion of biomedical research.
 
• It operates under the **Department of Health Research**, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India.
 
• ICMR plays a pivotal role in addressing public health challenges such as **infectious diseases, non-communicable diseases**, and **environmental health**.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Infectious Disease Research and Diagnostic Laboratory (IRDL):**
 
 
• IRDLs are crucial for the **early detection, diagnosis**, and management of infectious diseases.
 
• They help in identifying **emerging and re-emerging pathogens**, thereby aiding in outbreak preparedness and response.
 
• Such laboratories also facilitate **collaborative research** and contribute to the development of vaccines, therapeutics, and diagnostic tools.
 
 
 
• **Other Selected Institutes for IRDL:**

• **Emerging Infectious Diseases:**

• IRDLs are vital for studying **antimicrobial resistance (AMR)**, a growing public health challenge in India and globally.
 
 
 
• **Public Health Infrastructure in India:**
 
 
• ICMR’s efforts to establish IRDLs contribute to building a robust **disease surveillance system** and improving **healthcare delivery**.
 
• This initiative aligns with the Government of India’s vision of achieving **Universal Health Coverage (UHC)** and strengthening public health capacity.

questions.question: What major international goal does the High Seas Treaty aim to advance once in force?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Create marine protected areas**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **High Seas Treaty** is a landmark agreement developed under the **United Nations** to ensure the protection and sustainable use of marine biodiversity beyond national jurisdictions.
 
• One of the treaty's primary goals is to establish **marine protected areas (MPAs)** in regions beyond national waters, which cover nearly **two-thirds of the world's oceans**.
 
• These **marine protected areas** will help conserve biodiversity, protect endangered marine species, and ensure that ecosystems are resilient to climate change and human exploitation.
 
• The treaty emphasizes the regulation of activities like fishing, shipping, and deep-sea mining to reduce human-induced harm to marine ecosystems.
 
• The agreement aligns with the **30x30 conservation target**, which aims to protect **30% of the world's oceans** by the year **2030**, as part of global efforts to combat biodiversity loss.
 
• The treaty also promotes international collaboration for scientific research and equitable sharing of marine genetic resources.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Marine Protected Areas (MPAs):**

 
 
• **MPAs** are designated zones in oceans and seas where human activities are regulated to protect marine biodiversity and ecosystems.
 
• Examples include coral reef preservation, fish spawning areas, and habitats for endangered marine species such as whales and turtles.
 
• Globally, less than **10% of the oceans** are currently protected, necessitating stronger international efforts.
 
• MPAs contribute to sustainable fisheries, tourism, and carbon sequestration by preserving marine ecosystems.
 
 
 
• **Deep-Sea Mining:**
 
 
• Deep-sea mining involves extracting minerals from the ocean floor, such as **cobalt, nickel, and rare earth elements**, which are critical for technology manufacturing.
 
• However, this activity poses risks to marine biodiversity, including the destruction of fragile deep-sea habitats.
 
• Under the High Seas Treaty, deep-sea mining activities will be subject to stringent environmental assessments.
 
 
 
• **30x30 Conservation Target:**
 
 
• The **30x30 initiative** was adopted during the **2022 UN Biodiversity Conference (COP15)** in Montreal, Canada.
 
• It aims to protect **30% of terrestrial and marine ecosystems** by 2030 to halt biodiversity loss.
 
• The High Seas Treaty plays a crucial role in achieving this goal by focusing on ocean conservation beyond national jurisdictions.
 
 
 
• **Importance of International Collaboration:**
 
 
• The treaty fosters cooperation among nations to address global challenges like **overfishing, habitat destruction, and climate change**.
 
• It emphasizes equitable sharing of marine genetic resources, which are vital for pharmaceutical and scientific advancements.
 
• Scientific research under the treaty will help track ocean health and guide policy decisions.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **UN Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS):**

 
 
• The High Seas Treaty builds on the **UNCLOS framework**, which governs maritime activities and defines international waters.
 
• UNCLOS, established in **1982**, provides legal principles for ocean governance, but lacked provisions for high seas biodiversity conservation.
 
• The treaty addresses this gap by focusing on sustainability and environmental protection.
 
 
 
• **Threats to Marine Biodiversity:**
 
 
• **Overfishing:** Many fish populations are being exploited beyond sustainable levels.
 
• **Climate Change:** Rising sea temperatures and ocean acidification disrupt ecosystems and species survival.
 
• **Pollution:** Plastics and other pollutants harm marine life and degrade habitats.
 
• **Habitat Destruction:** Activities like trawling and mining damage fragile marine ecosystems.
 
 
 
• **Implementation Challenges:**
 
 
• Effective enforcement of the treaty will require significant financial and technological investments.
 
• Global coordination is essential to balance conservation goals with economic interests like fishing and shipping.

questions.question: Which wildlife area has been recently recognised as India’s 107th national park?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Similipal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Similipal National Park**, located in the state of **Odisha**, has recently been recognized as India’s **107th National Park**, adding to the country’s list of protected wildlife areas.
 
• Similipal derives its name from the abundance of **Simul trees (silk cotton trees)** found in the region.
 
• It was earlier designated as a **Tiger Reserve** in 1973 under Project Tiger and has been a **Biosphere Reserve** since 1994.
 
• This park is renowned for its rich biodiversity, which includes unique species such as the **Royal Bengal Tiger**, **Asian elephant**, and Indian bison, among others.
 
• The park also boasts **beautiful landscapes** and features **waterfalls** like Barehipani and Joranda, dense forests, and a variety of flora and fauna.
 
• Recognizing Similipal as a National Park strengthens its conservation status, ensuring further protection of its ecosystems and wildlife.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Similipal National Park Features:**

 
 
• Spread over an area of **2,750 square kilometers**, Similipal is one of the largest National Parks in India.
 
• The park hosts over **94 species of orchids** and more than **3,000 species of plants**, making it a haven for botanists.
 
• Similipal is home to over **55 mammal species**, **304 bird species**, **60 reptile species**, and numerous amphibians and insects.
 
• The park is part of the **Mayurbhanj district** in Odisha and forms an important part of the Eastern Ghats biodiversity hotspot.
 
 
 
• **Other National Parks in India:**
 
 
• India has a total of **107 National Parks**, and each plays a critical role in wildlife conservation.
 
• Some prominent National Parks include **Jim Corbett National Park** (Uttarakhand), **Kaziranga National Park** (Assam), **Sundarbans National Park** (West Bengal), and **Gir National Park** (Gujarat).
 
• Each park is vital for preserving the unique ecosystems and biodiversity of its region.
 
 
 
• **Importance of National Parks:**
 
 
• National Parks serve as protected areas to conserve **endangered species** and their habitats.
 
• They help in maintaining **ecological balance** and contribute to climate regulation.
 
• They provide opportunities for **eco-tourism**, promoting awareness and sustainable development.
 
• National Parks also play a significant role in **scientific research** and biodiversity studies.
 
 
 
• **Key Characteristics of Other Options:**
 
 
• **Buxa Tiger Reserve:** Located in West Bengal, it is known for its diverse fauna and is a critical tiger habitat.
 
• **Nagarhole National Park:** Situated in Karnataka, it is part of the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve and is famous for its population of tigers and elephants.
 
• **Palamau Tiger Reserve:** Located in Jharkhand, it is one of India’s first tiger reserves established under Project Tiger.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Legal Framework for National Parks:**

 
 
• National Parks are governed under the **Wildlife Protection Act of 1972**, ensuring legal protection for wildlife and their habitats.
 
• Activities like hunting, poaching, and deforestation are strictly prohibited in National Parks.
 
• The Ministry of Environment, Forest, and Climate Change oversees the management and expansion of National Parks.
 
 
 
• **Conservation Challenges:**
 
 
• Encroachment, deforestation, and human-wildlife conflicts are significant threats to National Parks.
 
• Climate change impacts biodiversity and ecosystems within protected areas.
 
• Government initiatives like Project Tiger and Project Elephant aim to address these challenges and strengthen conservation efforts.

• Provision for **remote voting** to facilitate voting for migrant workers and NRIs (Non-Resident Indians).
 
• Enhanced cybersecurity measures to prevent **data breaches** and ensure the integrity of election processes.

• **cVIGIL App:** An app for citizens to report violations of the Model Code of Conduct during elections.
 
• **Suvidha Portal:** A single-window platform for candidates and political parties to file nominations and track permissions.

questions.question: Which of the following institutes that was launched in May 2025 developed the Bharat Forecast System to give sharper rain alerts?

options.text: National Centre for Medium Range Weather Forecasting

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology (IITM)**, located in Pune, Maharashtra, is an autonomous institute under the Ministry of Earth Sciences, Government of India.
 
• The IITM launched the **Bharat Forecast System** in **May 2025** to provide more precise and localized rain alerts to address the challenges of weather prediction in India.
 
• This advanced system incorporates high-resolution numerical weather prediction models, which enable sharper and more accurate predictions of rainfall at regional and local levels.
 
• The system is particularly beneficial for sectors like agriculture, water resource management, and disaster preparedness, ensuring effective planning and mitigation of weather-related risks.
 
• The IITM is renowned for its contributions to weather and climate research, including monsoon studies, tropical cyclone predictions, and climate modeling, making it the ideal institution to develop such a system.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology (IITM):**

 
 
• Established in **1962**, the IITM is dedicated to research in tropical meteorology and climate systems.
 
• The institute is involved in the development of advanced weather forecasting tools and models, including monsoon prediction systems.
 
• It plays a pivotal role in understanding and addressing climate variability, air pollution, and atmospheric processes in the tropics.
 
• One of its flagship projects includes the **Monsoon Mission**, which aims to improve monsoon forecasting capabilities in India.
 
 
 
• **Bharat Forecast System:**
 
 
• Launched by the IITM in **2025**, this system is designed to provide **real-time, high-resolution weather forecasts**.
 
• It incorporates cutting-edge technology such as machine learning, satellite data assimilation, and advanced computational models.
 
• Its primary focus is to provide accurate rainfall predictions, which are critical for agriculture, urban planning, and disaster management.
 
• The system also supports early warning systems for extreme weather events, enhancing India's disaster response capabilities.
 
 
 
• **Other Relevant Organizations:**
 
 
• **India Meteorological Department (IMD):** Responsible for weather forecasts, early warnings, and cyclone tracking in India.
 
• **Indian Institute of Science (IISc):** Focuses on scientific research and advanced studies, contributing to atmospheric and climate sciences.
 
• **National Centre for Medium Range Weather Forecasting (NCMRWF):** Specializes in medium-range weather predictions and model development.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Advanced Weather Forecasting:**
 
 
• Improved agricultural planning and yield prediction.
 
• Enhanced flood and drought management strategies.
 
• Better urban planning and infrastructure development.
 
• Strengthened disaster preparedness and mitigation efforts.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Why Accurate Rainfall Prediction is Crucial:**

 
 
• India's economy is largely agrarian, with over **50% of the population** dependent on agriculture, which is highly sensitive to rainfall variability.
 
• Extreme weather events such as floods, droughts, and cyclones cause significant damage to infrastructure, crops, and livelihoods.
 
• Accurate weather forecasts enable governments and communities to take proactive measures to minimize losses.
 
 
 
• **Recent Developments in Weather Forecasting:**
 
 
• India has invested in advanced technologies such as **Doppler weather radars**, satellite systems, and supercomputers for enhanced forecasting.
 
• Programs like the **National Monsoon Mission** have significantly improved India's ability to predict monsoon patterns.
 
• Collaboration with international organizations, such as the **World Meteorological Organization (WMO)**, has bolstered India's weather prediction capabilities.
